goal: Lock the cardinality-independent N-profile by M-surface product contract and the no-redesign boundary.

goal: Correct and revalidate the declaration-derived N-profile by M-surface architecture before integration resumes.
description: Scope: Requirements.md, Evidence.md, Architecture.md, Validation.md, Delivery-Evidence.md, production profile/surface discovery, composition, boundary verification, and frozen-design evidence. Context: a follow-up audit found that fixed observed inventory assumptions and prior closure receipts cannot serve as the architecture contract. Target: derive N from the canonical profile registrations with directory-set equality, derive M from the typed runtime-surface declaration, construct and validate exactly N×M bundles, and make all consumers and gates cardinality-independent. Design Considerations: use immutable declaration-derived maps and exact-set validation; treat directory enumeration as an ownership check rather than a second identity authority; keep shared boundaries semantic and style-free; generate transitive and pairwise checks from discovered sets. Design Value: adding or removing a profile or runtime surface changes only its owning declarations and private bundles while management, Settings, host, and verifier algorithms remain unchanged. Constraints & Risks: preserve the currently rendered visuals; prohibit shared styled chrome, shared complete controllers, behavioral or styling branches on profile ID, manual profile identity inventories, fixed-count assertions, compatibility paths, and unverified completion claims.

acceptance_criteria.text: Living plan artifacts define N from canonical profile registration plus directory-set equality, M from the typed runtime-surface declaration, and exact N×M coverage; any observed numeric values are labeled one-run evidence only.

Composition and verification discover arbitrary profile and surface sets, reject missing or extra Cartesian-product members, and pass synthetic add-profile and add-surface mutations without consumer-algorithm edits.

Transitive boundary checks reject shared styled chrome, shared complete-controller access, sibling-profile imports, behavioral or styling branches on profile ID, and every manually maintained second profile identity inventory.

Every surface-declared destination is carried by an immutable snapshot and narrow action port keyed by surface and destination; LayoutHost owns the active typed lease, every complete styled destination tree is profile/surface-private, and the widget-producing content port plus shared presentation scope are absent.

Comparison-only visual, semantics, key, and interaction evidence proves every dynamically discovered bundle preserves its frozen current design without refreshing the baseline after the correction starts.
Post-correction evidence reruns the scoped layout, boundary, manifest, Better Plan validation, and requirement-label gates without relying on historical fixed-inventory receipts.
